cards.title: Product Feed Optimization Basics for Google Merchant Center
cards.summary: Keep feed titles, descriptions and images simple and accurate, sync availability automatically, and never edit sale price inside GMC.
cards.use_when: Optimizing your Google Merchant Center product feed so Shopping and PMax ads can serve correctly and convert.
steps: Do not overcomplicate feed titles, descriptions or images; the source argues keeping them simple and accurate works best and that most people overcomplicate this.
Never change your sale price inside Google Merchant Center itself — leave pricing to sync from your store so no mismatch can appear.
Make availability dynamic to real stock: anything out of stock must be marked sold out, or Google will flag you for showing 'in stock and ready to ship'.
Do the same pass across every SKU; note that scaling this is mostly manual work if you have many SKUs, but once correct it improves Shopping results.
caveats: The source claims results improve 'massively' but gives no measured benchmark — treat as directional.
GMC interface and feed rules change; verify current fields in the Merchant Center UI before editing.

cards.title: Payment and Checkout Compliance Checks for GMC
cards.summary: Test payment methods, final price transparency, and discount codes on your checkout, because GMC bots audit all three.
cards.use_when: Preparing or auditing your store checkout to avoid Google Merchant Center suspension or promotion disapproval.
steps: Maintain SSL on checkout pages — confirm the checkout URL starts with HTTPS, which Google requires for secure transactions.
Test every payment method you list (PayPal, cards, crypto, Afterpay, etc.); listing a method that doesn't actually work at checkout is a GMC error and can suspend the account.

Verify final price transparency: taxes, state-level sales tax, and shipping fees by destination must all be reflected before payment and match the Shopify and GMC data. Run test orders to confirm calculations.
Test discount code functionality. A promotion won't go live in GMC unless the code applies at checkout; if an approved promotion stops working, that is a big flag.
caveats: GMC's checkout audit behaviour is described from the presenter's experience, not official documentation; verify current policy.
Promotion approval rules and deadlines change — check GMC help docs.

cards.title: Listing Accuracy Checklist: Claims, Reviews, Links, Pricing
cards.summary: Make listing claims factual, reviews authentic, links correct and listed prices match checkout to prevent GMC misrepresentation flags.
cards.use_when: Auditing product listings and product pages before scaling Google Shopping or PMax spend.
steps: Review product claims for accuracy and remove exaggerated or unverifiable claims; stick to factual benefits. If making scientific claims, provide credible resources in listings, descriptions and on the landing page.
Verify review authenticity and recency. The presenter warns against fake reviews; he recommends a real review flow and pushing a review feed into GMC so star ratings show on Shopping listings.
Mark out-of-stock items as sold out and keep availability dynamic to real inventory — showing 'in stock and ready to ship' on an out-of-stock item is a violation.
Check every link, especially product page to shopping listing; broken or mismatched links can be flagged as a scam and lead to suspension.
Ensure listed price matches checkout price and discounts apply accurately; mismatches cause abandoned carts and GMC disapprovals.
caveats: The source calls unverifiable claims 'the biggest thing that hits brands' — his experience, not a published statistic.
Claim rules vary by category (e.g. health); confirm current Google misrepresentation policy.

cards.title: Branding, Navigation and Legal Page Checks for GMC
cards.summary: Polish brand assets, keep footer links working and update legal pages to look like a reputable store in Google's eyes.
cards.use_when: Cleaning up store branding, navigation and policy pages so GMC bots see a trusted store.
steps: Optimize logo quality and placement and complete all brand information plus URL and business verification in GMC during setup.
Update homepage branding, messaging and visuals monthly — also a CRO move, but it keeps the store looking reputable rather than like a default theme.
Check navigation and hamburger menu for broken links and direct links to contact, home, products, about, return policy, shipping policy and subscription management. Google bots crawl these.
Review and update terms and conditions and ensure the privacy policy reflects current data practices; Shopify provides defaults to start from.
Test all footer links so return, about, terms of service, contact, shipping and subscription management policies are reachable from the footer, where Google verifies trust.
caveats: The source calls branding 'low leverage' for suspension risk but still worth doing.
Default theme usage is described as a trust signal risk — opinion, not a stated Google rule.

cards.title: Shipping, Returns and Contact Info Sync for GMC
cards.summary: Keep shipping costs, courier details, returns policy and contact info synchronized between your site and GMC and review them monthly.
cards.use_when: Setting up or maintaining shipping, returns and contact sections to prevent GMC suspension.
steps: Match website shipping settings to GMC shipping and returns sections, including shipping cost and delivery times. The source shares a client case where shipping cost dropped after a courier change but GMC wasn't updated, causing a week-long suspension.
Name the courier services you actually use (UPS, FedEx, DHL) in both your shipping policy page and GMC shipping policy.
Confirm order tracking functionality works and that the courier provides tracking; customer service will feel it otherwise.

Write clear step-by-step return instructions in both your site returns policy and GMC, and link GMC to the site returns page. Missing returns, shipping or terms pages guarantees suspension per the source.
Update refund processing timings monthly, keep return periods current, test return links, and verify return address and timing monthly.

Verify physical business address monthly, test the customer service phone number, use a branded domain email (not Gmail), and cross-check contact details match across GMC, Google Ads and all Google accounts.
caveats: The week-long suspension is one client example, not a benchmark.
The claim that a phone number is required is softened by the source to 'or at least an easy way to contact you' — treat as preference.

cards.title: Site Speed, Design and App Health as GMC Trust Signals
cards.summary: Fast, well-branded sites with working apps get better CPCs and store ratings; slow or broken stores risk GMC penalties.
cards.use_when: Improving site experience to protect Google Ads performance and Merchant Center standing.
steps: Test website loading speed and optimize user navigation paths. A slow site causes bounces, wastes paid clicks, and the source says Google marks you down versus competitors in CPCs and can cost you the trusted seller badge.
Update store design so it is properly branded and official: avoid default themes, use high-quality non-AI-generated images and clear fonts.
Make product images and descriptions congruent with what is shown in GMC — this helps conversion rate and keeps Google's view consistent.
Test all apps and plugins for functionality. Dead apps slow the store; broken actively-used apps create user-experience flags that escalate to GMC risk.
caveats: Slow-site CPC penalty and badge loss are the source's claims about Google behaviour; verify against current Google documentation.
No specific speed threshold is given.

cards.title: The 34-Item GMC Anti-Suspension Checklist by Frequency
cards.summary: Work a 34-point Google Merchant Center checklist split into daily, weekly, monthly and one-time tasks to avoid suspension.
cards.use_when: Building an ongoing ops routine for your Google Merchant Center account.
steps: Organize checks into the source's categories: payment and checkout, product listings, branding, shipping information, returns, legal compliance, contact info, and store design/performance.
Assign each item a frequency — daily, weekly, monthly or once — and actually do once-tasks during GMC setup (URL and business verification, branded email, terms defaults, SSL).
Do the full checklist deliberately rather than quickly: the presenter says pause, check each item in your GMC, and change it immediately if missing.
If you get suspended, assume it is one of these 34 items, since Google typically won't tell you the exact cause.
Keep the list as a living document and re-run it after any change to shipping, pricing or fulfilment suppliers.
caveats: The source calls the result 'bulletproof' and 'basically guaranteed' — that is confidence framing, not a guarantee.
Checklist content and GMC policy change; verify against current GMC help docs.

cards.title: Build a Reusable Brand Context Profile with AI Before Writing Ad Copy
cards.summary: Train an LLM on your brand and product page to produce a reusable context profile for ads, landing pages and emails.
cards.use_when: Preparing to generate Google Ads assets, Meta copy, landing page copy or emails and needing consistent brand context.
steps: Give the AI a role, context, task, examples, constraints and desired output — the source calls this the best way to prompt anything.
Use a prompt casting the AI as a world-class direct response copywriter for ecommerce cold traffic, and feed it a PDF of a product page (e.g. save the page as PDF from the browser).

Have it audit the page for value proposition, emotional and logical persuasion, CTAs, voice of customer, proof mechanisms, offer positioning, copy structure, conversion blockers and missed psychological levers, plus optimization suggestions.

Run a second prompt casting it as an elite advertising strategist/deep researcher to map product intelligence, customer psychographics, competitors, keyword and intent mapping, and market positioning.
Save the resulting context profile offline or in Drive so you and your team can reuse it for any asset type.
caveats: The source has his own prompt pack; prompts shown are his workflow, not universal.
AI output quality depends on input quality — garbage in, garbage out.

cards.title: Use AI Deep Research to Build Customer and Market Understanding
cards.summary: Run a deep research prompt in a research-capable model with your URL and product PDF to produce a long brand, audience and market brief.
cards.use_when: Replacing or supplementing weeks of manual customer and market research before writing ads or landing pages.
steps: Use AI to write the deep research prompt itself: instruct a prompt-engineer persona to produce a single detailed prompt for an elite advertising strategist covering brand, audience, positioning, product and voice.
Paste that prompt into a deep research tool with web access plus your store URL and the product page PDF.
Expect roughly 15–20 minutes of runtime; the source notes the tool shows its research trail (Reddit, YouTube, etc.), which can surface authentic voice-of-customer language.
Export the output (often 30+ pages) to Google Drive and archive it so you can update it later.
Mine the output for angles, offers, reframing, emotional and logical buy triggers and audience awareness levels before writing copy.
caveats: Presenter says Google's deep research is currently best and that this may go out of date; he also says this gets you about 80% of the way there, not 100%.
Tool choice and capabilities change quickly — verify current options.

cards.title: Convert Research into JSON Context Profiles for Consistent Copy
cards.summary: Use an LLM to turn deep research into avatar, market and brand JSON profiles plus one combined context file.
cards.use_when: Structuring brand research so any AI session can instantly understand your store before generating copy.
steps: Prompt a strong writing model (the source uses Claude Sonnet 4) as a world-class AI prompt engineer and brand strategist, feeding it the full deep research document.

Have it produce four outputs: a customer avatar JSON, a market context JSON (pricing tiers, direct and indirect competitors, target keywords, competitive landscape), a brand context JSON, and a full combined context profile.
Use the combined profile as the paste-in context for any model when generating ad copy, landing pages or emails.
Keep the JSON files in Drive so your whole team can reuse them; note that long responses may pause and require 'continue'.
Expect detail like avatar psychographics, competitor mapping and offer positioning — the point is precision, not brevity.
caveats: JSON is used because it maps variables clearly for LLMs; it is a workflow choice, not a Google requirement.
Model names and best-model recommendations may change.

cards.title: Generate All Google Ads Assets from a Context Profile
cards.summary: Paste your brand context plus a Google Ads JSON asset template into an LLM to produce RSA headlines, descriptions, sitelinks, callouts, snippets and PMax assets.
cards.use_when: Building Google Search or PMax campaign assets at scale without starting from a blank page.
steps: Load the full context profile into a fresh model session together with the Google Ads asset JSON template.
Prompt simply: create all the Google Ads assets needed for my brand.

Review outputs organized as Search and PMax assets — headlines (including long ones), descriptions, sitelinks, callouts, structured snippets, price extension suggestions, and asset variations by awareness level (problem, solution, product, most aware) plus competitor and responsive search ad examples.
Ask for a product feed Shopping title when needed; the model returns primary and alternative titles, keyword-optimized and competitive variations, promotional titles, and explains why they work.
Manually edit weak or off-brand lines — the source flags examples like 'aerospace grade materials' as bad and 'stop buying cheap wallets' as possibly off-brand.
caveats: The source says AI gets you roughly 80–90% of the way; human judgment supplies the rest.
The '$10M new customer revenue' figure is the agency's claim about its workflow, not a guaranteed result.
Verify character limits and current asset requirements in Google Ads.

cards.title: Set Up a Branded Search Campaign to Protect and Capture Demand
cards.summary: Run a search campaign on exact-match brand terms with impression-share bidding to own the SERP, defend against competitors and feed cheap conversion data.
cards.use_when: Launching or optimizing paid search on your own brand name to capture searchers who saw you elsewhere.
steps: Create a Search campaign, optimize for the purchase conversion, name it clearly (agency + brand + 'search brand').

Use impression share bidding, not conversions, and set 'absolute top of search' to about 95%, with a max CPC around $3. In the source's experience brand clicks then cost about 1–2 cents, at most around 50 cents.
Turn off search and display network partners, target your own country using presence (not presence or interest), set English, and add observational audiences like customer list and GA traffic.
Add exact-match brand keywords such as [brand], [brand reviews], [brand discount code]; optionally add phrase match versions of best exact-match keywords for extra scope.
Write RSAs with brand + 'official site' + offer headlines and sales copy descriptions; add logo and business name; set a daily budget like $25.
Optimize by raising max CPC only if the budget won't spend, and never switch away from absolute top of search.
caveats: The source says you are often paying for some conversions that might have happened organically, but argues the space, defence and cheap conversion-data benefits justify it.
The $64 spend returning $1.5K and $858 returning 24 orders are specific examples, not benchmarks.
CPC and bidding options change — verify current Google Ads settings.

cards.title: Why Every Ecommerce Brand Should Run a Branded Search Campaign
cards.summary: Branded search ads expand your SERP footprint, defend your brand from competitors and load cheap high-intent conversion data into your account.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to spend on your own brand terms in Google Ads.
steps: Take up more SERP space: paid ad at top plus organic results plus Shopping results leaves searchers surrounded by your brand.
Defend your branded term from competitors who may bid on it with 'us vs them' ads; the source says running early helps Google give you ad rank as the official advertiser.
Induce purchases from people who discovered you on Facebook or organic content and then search your name — an offer in the ad can move them from research to buying.
Feed your purchase conversion action with cheap, high-intent conversions that improve performance of Shopping, PMax and other campaigns.
Add buying-journey safety: a sponsored 'official site' result helps searchers trust they are on the real store rather than a knockoff or scammer.
caveats: SAS is where the source says competitor brand-bidding is most prevalent; ecommerce less so.
The source concedes most brand conversions would often happen organically anyway — the case is marginal gain and defence, not pure incremental revenue.

cards.title: Set Up and Automate a Branded Shopping Campaign with Scripts
cards.summary: Create a Shopping campaign limited to branded terms and use scripts to automatically exclude non-branded search queries.
cards.use_when: Adding a high-leverage, fast-to-launch Shopping campaign to lift account efficiency and cheap sales.
steps: Duplicate or build a Shopping campaign structure, then exclude all non-branded terms so it only serves on branded queries.
Use a negative keyword script to automatically keep non-branded queries out of the campaign as search terms accumulate.
Match product feed titles and descriptions to brand naming so the campaign surfaces on brand searches.
Monitor and adjust exclusions regularly to prevent non-branded spend leaking into the branded campaign.
The source says this can be set up in a couple of clicks and lift ROAS and spend efficiency within about 24 hours.
caveats: The claim of uplift within 24 hours is the presenter's description, not a measured benchmark.
Script availability and Shopping campaign structure can change — verify current Google Ads interface and script sources.
